children.text: idānīm ātmabhuvā kriyamāṇe saptatantau tatsādhanatvenānirvacanīyasukhodbodhahetutvena vāruṇīprāśanam anudarśayati ananyajasaptatantāv iti ||
children.translated_text: Now, in the seven-stranded sacrifice being performed by the Self-born one, he indicates the drinking of <s>vāruṇī</s> either as a means to that or as the cause of the awakening of an indescribable pleasure, in the words 'in the seven-stranded rite of the one not born from another.'

children.text: anutṛṣyanti anirvacanīyānandaṃ prāpnuvanti anenety anutarṣaṃ kādambaraṃ tasya svīkaraṇam anuprāśanaṃ tasya prāśanasyātyāvaśyakatvam atīva īpsitatamatvam anirvacanīyānandapradātṛtvena retaḥstambhakatvena hetunā karmānuṣṭhānāt pūrvaṃ pracetasaḥ kanyāyāḥ svīkaraṇaṃ kartavyam ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'That by which they thirst after, that is, attain, indescribable bliss' is <s>anutarṣa</s>, namely kādambara wine. Its acceptance is the subsequent drinking of it. The extreme necessity of that drinking, its being most intensely desired, means this: because it bestows indescribable delight and restrains semen, the daughter of <s>Pracetas</s> should be accepted before the performance of the act.
The <s>Amara</s> says: '<s>Makaradhvaja</s> is <s>Ātmabhū</s>.'
The <s>Amara</s> says: 'The seven-stranded one is a sacrifice, a rite.'

children.text: nanu anutarṣasvīkaraṇam adṛṣṭaphalodbodhe upakārakam āhosvit dṛṣṭaphalodbodhe upakārakaṃ veti saṃśayavākyam upanyasya dṛṣṭaphalodbodhe eva sākṣād upakārakaṃ na kiṃcit svargādiphalavat ānuśravikavākyaṃ kalpyam upakārakam iti manasi niścitya pūrvasūtrasya hetutvena dvitīyaṃ sūtram anuśāsti ||
children.translated_text: Having introduced a sentence of doubt, namely whether the acceptance of <s>anutarṣa</s> assists in awakening an unseen result or in awakening a seen result, and having resolved in his mind that it directly assists only in awakening a seen result, and that no scriptural sentence such as one concerning heaven and the like need be imagined as its auxiliary, he teaches the second sūtra as the reason for the preceding sūtra.
'Of the pleasure of love' is the phrase.
It should be understood as meaning, 'when the acceptance of <s>anutarṣa</s> has taken place.'

children.text: anena vākyena anayoḥ kāryakāraṇasaṃgatiḥ upapāditā bhavati tathā cāyam arthaḥ anutarṣasvīkaraṇe kṛte sati nidhuvanavyāpāre ratyānando 'nirvacanīya utpadyate netarathā sāmudrikaṇāmiśritasya sūpaśākādidravyasyeva nīrasaḥ svāduḥ prādurbhūyate ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By this sentence the relation of cause and effect between the two is established. Accordingly, this is the meaning: when the acceptance of <s>anutarṣa</s> has taken place, an indescribable pleasure of love arises in the act of intercourse; otherwise a tasteless flavor appears, as in soup, greens, and other substances not mixed with salt.

children.text: anyad apy anirvacanīyam upakārāntaraṃ tṛtīyasūtreṇa anuśāsti saṃpradarśayati ||
children.translated_text: He teaches and shows another indescribable additional benefit by means of the third sūtra.
'At the arising of <s>udañji</s>' is the phrase.

children.text: pāśinaḥ ātmajayā saha atiprītyupacayena tādātmyabhāvaṃ gamite sati nimittakāraṇasyātyupakārakatayā taddvārā svakīyānandasyānirvacanīyāhlāde prayojakībhūtaṃ bhavatīty arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the noose-bearer, together with his own wife, has been brought into a state of identity through an excessive increase of delight, then, because the instrumental cause is extremely beneficial, through that channel it becomes productive of an indescribable exhilaration in his own bliss. This is the meaning.

children.text: anena vākyenātyāvaśyakatayā tādṛgvyāpārasya purastāt tādṛṅnirveśanaṃ sampādya tatpurastāt saptatantoḥ karmādhikāre 'dhikāritā itarathā nimittakāraṇe utsāhaśaktibhraṃśāt sākalyena narmavyāpāradhvaṃso bhavatīty arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By this sentence the meaning is this: because it is utterly necessary, such insertion is to be accomplished before such activity, and only after that is there eligibility for the sacrificial office of the seven-stranded rite; otherwise, because the energy and power fail in the instrumental cause, the playful activity is wholly destroyed.
He shows the settled conclusion of this sūtra.
'When the object to be impelled is principal' is the phrase.

children.text: prayojyasyodañjeḥ prādhānyakartṛtvam abhyutthāne sati sampadyate tadabhāve abhyutthānābhāve nimittāpāye naimittikasyāpy apāya iti nyāyena ratitantraṃ lupyate kutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When rising has occurred, the principal agency of the object to be impelled, namely <s>udañji</s>, is accomplished. In its absence, that is, in the absence of rising, the system of love collapses, because by the maxim 'when the cause is absent, the effect too is absent,' the causal condition is gone. How could it not?

children.text: nimittakāraṇasyābhāvāt yathā turīvemādisattve paṭakāryasyotpattir netarathā tathā abhyutthānasattve tantravidhānasyotpattiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because the instrumental cause is absent. Just as, when the shuttle, loom, and the like exist, the effect called cloth arises, and not otherwise, so too, when rising exists, the arrangement of the system arises.

children.text: anena vākyenātyāvaśyakatvenānutarṣasvīkaraṇaṃ sampādya tatpurastāt nidhuvanavyāpāre pravṛttir vidheyā iti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By this sentence the intended sense is that, after the acceptance of <s>anutarṣa</s> has been accomplished as something utterly necessary, engagement in the act of intercourse is to be enjoined thereafter.

children.text: idānīṃ sūtracatuṣṭayasya sākalyena kṛtsnaṃ tātparyārthaṃ saṃgṛhya avyabhicaritaṃ sarvasūtrāṇāṃ rāddhāntavākyaṃ saṃpradarśayati ||
children.translated_text: Now, having gathered together the complete purport of the four sūtras as a whole, he presents the invariable sentence of conclusion for all the sūtras.
'When the playful activity is expanded in the object to be impelled' is the phrase.

children.text: pūrvasmin sūtre vāhyatantre yat kiṃcid avacchedenādhikārikatvaṃ nirūpitam asmin sūtre tu prayojakasya sākalyena narmapravṛttinimittasyābhāve jāyamāne sati prayojyavyāpāre 'pi atyantābhāvasya vidhānaṃ nirvyavasāyenaiva prāptaṃ bhavati kiṃcid viśeṣavidhānaṃ yatra nopalabhyata iti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the preceding sūtra, eligibility in the external system was described with some limitation. In this sūtra, however, when the impelling cause of the entire playful activity is absent, the prescription of total absence even in the activity of the object to be impelled is obtained with certainty; no special prescription is found anywhere. This is the intended sense.

children.text: tasmād anutarṣasvīkaraṇād anantaram eva narmakarmādhikāre ādhikārikatvam iti pañcasūtrāṇām eka eva tātparyārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the single purport of the five sūtras is this: immediately after the acceptance of <s>anutarṣa</s>, there is eligibility for the office of the amorous act.

children.text: māghakirātaraghuvaṃśeṣu siddhāntitasya vākyasyaivāyam anuvādaḥ na tv apūrvavidhānaṃ svamanīṣayā upakalpya proktam iti śaṅkanīyam ||
children.translated_text: One should not suspect that this was stated by imagining some unprecedented injunction through his own cleverness; rather, it is merely a restatement of a proposition established in <s>Māgha</s>, the <s>Kirāta</s>, and the <s>Raghuvaṃśa</s>.

children.text: kiṃca dvitīyāvasthām atikrāntasya diṣṭyātmajāyayā saha asaṃstutapremaprāduṣkaraṇe saṃyuktasya janasya saprakārakarasotpattyanubhave tādṛṅmanīṣāyā abhāvāt sīdhusaṃgrahaṇaṃ paramakāraṇatvena nābhimatam taditarāvasthāyāṃ tu andhasaḥ śamalasya anirvacanīyānandaprakāśane svīkaraṇatvena saṃgrahaṇam atyāvaśyakatvenābhimatam eva īdṛksaṃvidā yāthārthyajñānaṃ parikalpya tādṛkkarmādhikāre anutarṣasvīkaraṇam atyāvaśyakatamam iti narmavyāpārakartṝṇām āptavākyavat yathārthopadeśam anuśāsti ||
children.translated_text: Moreover, for a person who has passed beyond the second stage and who, by good fortune, is joined with his own wife in the manifestation of unstudied love, the taking of liquor is not considered the supreme cause in the experience of rasa arising in its full varieties, because such intention is absent. But in the other stage, when food or drink manifests indescribable pleasure from the impurity, its taking is indeed regarded as utterly necessary in the form of acceptance. Having imagined true knowledge through such an awareness, he teaches that the acceptance of <s>anutarṣa</s> is most necessary for eligibility in such an act, as a truthful instruction like the authoritative word of those who perform amorous activity.
'In the sport of the system of love' is the phrase.

children.text: ratitantravilāse narmavyāpāravilāse anirvacanīyarasotpattau ṣaḍvidharasād atirikto yo rasaḥ amṛtāndhasām upabhogayogya iti yāvat kādambararasasya anuprāśanasya paramakāraṇatvam tādṛgrase sampīte sati nidhuvanavyāpāravistāre rasabhāvanāviśeṣacaturāṇām anirvacanīyasukhodbodhaṃ janayatīty arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the delight of the system of love, in the delight of amorous play, when an indescribable rasa arises, the rasa that is beyond the six kinds of rasa, that is, fit to be enjoyed by those who feed on nectar, is the supreme cause of sipping the taste of kādambara. When such a rasa has been thoroughly drunk, in the expansion of the act of intercourse it produces an awakening of indescribable pleasure in those skilled in the special cultivation of rasa. This is the meaning.
Moreover, he shows another special, indescribable rasa by the drinking of liquor.
'In the formation of graceful coquettish movements' is the phrase.
The <s>Amara</s> says: '<s>Puṣkara</s> means facing in all directions.'

children.text: puṣkarādhipateḥ ātmajāyāḥ lalitavibhramabandhaprāduṣkaraṇaṃ naisargikaḥ svabhāva iti sūtrārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The meaning of the sūtra is that the manifestation of formations of graceful coquettish movement is the natural disposition of the daughter of the lord of <s>Puṣkara</s>.

children.text: atra puṣkarādhipatiśabdena pratīcyāḥ kāṣṭhāyāḥ adhipatir lakṣyate tasya ātmajāyāḥ vāruṇyā anuprāśane kriyamāṇe lalitavibhramabandhānāṃ prakaṭīkaraṇe prayojikā bhavati netarathā kṛtsnavāṅmayasyādhidaivikarūpatvāt nirvyavasāyenaiva antaḥkaraṇasyāhlādakāḥ rucikaraprabandhāḥ atalapradeśāt kamalaniḥsaraṇam iva prāśanakartur mukhapadmanīḍāt prādurbhūyanta ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Here, by the word 'lord of <s>Puṣkara</s>' the lord of the western quarter is indicated; when the sipping of his daughter, <s>Vāruṇī</s>, is performed, she becomes the agent in making manifest formations of graceful coquettish movement, and not otherwise. Since all speech has a divine presiding form, delightful and charming compositions arise from the lotus-nest of the drinker's mouth, without deliberate effort of the mind, as a lotus emerges from the nether region. This is the meaning.

children.text: idam eva rasaviśeṣāntaraṃ saṃnipatyopakārakanyāyena paramāpūrvasādhane prayojakībhūtaṃ kāraṇaṃ nirbandhavarṇānāṃ śravaṇamātreṇa taddvārā manasijodbodhe anirvacanīyasādhanatvena paramakāraṇatvam ayam eva tasyāḥ naisargikasvabhāva iti ||
children.translated_text: This very other special rasa, as a cause that assists by conjunction and that becomes productive in the accomplishment of the highest unprecedented result, is the supreme cause, through that channel, for awakening <s>Manasija</s> merely by hearing the compulsory syllables, because it is an indescribable means. This alone is her natural disposition.
He shows yet another benefit by the following sūtra.
'With one near the dark stage' is the phrase.

children.text: śyāmāvasthāyā upa samīpe vartate sā upaśyāmā tayā caturdaśapañcadaśahāyanātmikayā yoṣayā saha madhuvārā madhupānāvṛttiḥ udañjidhārṣṭye atyantadṛḍhataratve prayojako bhavati anena vākyena parisaṃkhyāvidheḥ svarūpaṃ prakāśitaṃ bhavati ||
children.translated_text: She who is near the dark stage is <s>upaśyāmā</s>. With such a woman, one fourteen or fifteen years old, a <s>madhuvāra</s>, a recurrence of drinking liquor, becomes a cause of <s>udañji</s>-boldness, that is, of extreme firmness. By this sentence the nature of the rule of exclusion is made clear.

children.text: tathā cāyam arthaḥ atikrāntāvasthayā saha madhuvāre jāyamāne udañjidhārṣṭyaṃ naivotpadyate tayā saha tādṛgvyavasāyaḥ vaiyarthyatāṃ pratipadyate nyubjaghaṭopari jalapūraṇanyāyena tasmāt ratitantravilāse udañjidhārṣṭye manīṣāvatā puruṣeṇa galitayauvanayā saha madhuvāro naiva kartavya ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Accordingly, this is the meaning: when a <s>madhuvāra</s> occurs with a woman whose stage has passed, <s>udañji</s>-boldness simply does not arise; such an undertaking with her becomes futile, on the maxim of filling water over an inverted pot. Therefore, in the delight of the system of love, a discerning man should not perform <s>madhuvāra</s> with a woman whose youth has faded, for the sake of <s>udañji</s>-boldness. This is the meaning.

children.text: nirarthakaprayāse kasyāpi matir naivotpadyata iti nyāyāt ||
children.translated_text: For no one's mind arises toward a useless effort, according to the maxim.

children.text: dhanvantaryādīnāṃ matam anusṛtya kāpiśāyanasvīkaraṇe 'nirvacanīyāhlādadyotakam upakārāntaram anudarśayati ||
children.translated_text: Following the opinion of <s>Dhanvantari</s> and others, he shows another benefit, one that reveals indescribable delight, in the acceptance of <s>kāpiśāyana</s>.
'With a dark woman' is the phrase.

children.text: ṣoḍaśavārṣikī śyāmeti vātsyāyanasūtre prasiddhiḥ tādṛgavasthayā yoṣayā saha niveśanaṃ pānaṃ patiṣu nirviviśur madam aṅganā ity atra nirveśanaśabde pānaṃ lakṣyate yāmapramāṇaṃ yāmadvayasaṃ pramāṇe dvayasaj iti sūtreṇa pramāṇārthe dvayasacpratyayaḥ tādṛkpramāṇopalakṣite diṣṭe kāle kālo diṣṭopyanehāpīti kośasmaraṇāt tāvatkālam abhivyāpyeti yāvat retaḥstambhane paramakāraṇam iti tayā saha kāpiśāyanasya svīkaraṇe kriyamāṇe ekayāmaparyantaṃ varāṅgopari vrīhikaṇḍanavat āghātaṃ karotīty arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the sūtra of <s>Vātsyāyana</s>, the tradition is that a sixteen-year-old is called <s>śyāmā</s>. With a woman in such a stage, <s>niveśana</s> means drinking; in 'the women enjoyed intoxication among their husbands,' the word <s>nirveśana</s> indicates drinking. The measure is a <s>yāma</s>; by the sūtra 'when the measure is two yāmas, the affix <s>dvayasac</s>,' the affix <s>dvayasac</s> is used in the sense of measure. In the appointed time marked by such a measure, since the dictionary statement is remembered, 'time is also called <s>diṣṭa</s> and <s>anehas</s>,' that is, extending through that much time, it is the supreme cause of semen-retention. Thus, when acceptance of <s>kāpiśāyana</s> is performed with her, for the duration of one <s>yāma</s> one strikes upon the excellent limb as if pounding rice. This is the meaning.

children.text: idānīṃ narmavyāpāravistāre 'paricitanarmasukhānandāya nidhuvanāt pūrvaṃ kāpiśāyanaprāśanaṃ narmakhedāpanuttaye 'tyāvaśyakatvenānudarśayati ||
children.translated_text: Now, in the expansion of amorous play, for the sake of the joy of pleasure in unfamiliar dalliance, he shows that before intercourse the drinking of <s>kāpiśāyana</s> is absolutely necessary for removing the fatigue of love-play.
'The excellent limb without body-hair' is the phrase.

children.text: nirgataṃ tanūruhaṃ yasmāt tat nistanūruhaṃ tanūruhāṇāṃ prādurbhāveṇa rahitaṃ tac ca tat varāṅgaṃ ca tasya sambhedanaṃ svakīyenodañjinā mukhavidāraṇaṃ tādṛkkarmaṇi kriyamāṇe ajñātanarmavyāpārāyaireyaprāśanaṃ kārayitavyam kṛte aireyaprāśane manasijasadmavidīrṇavyathā sambhedakāle nānubhūyate itarathā sadmavidīrṇajanyavyathayā sadmani sthitānāṃ nāḍīnāṃ viparyāsena vyānavāyau saṃkaṭavyathā atitarām anubhūyate tadvyathānivāraṇārthaṃ nidhuvanāt pūrvaṃ dvipalapramāṇaṃ kāpiśāyanaṃ pāyayitavyam ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That from which body-hair has gone out is 'without body-hair,' meaning devoid of the manifestation of body-hairs; and that same thing is the excellent limb. Its penetration, the splitting open by one's own <s>udañji</s>, is the act in question. When such an act is being performed, a person unacquainted with amorous play should be made to drink <s>aireya</s>. Once the drinking of <s>aireya</s> has been done, the pain produced by the tearing of the abode of <s>Manasija</s> is not felt at the time of penetration. Otherwise, because of the pain produced by the tearing of the abode, and because the channels situated in the abode are disturbed, severe constricting pain is felt in the vital wind <s>vyāna</s>. In order to prevent that pain, before intercourse one should make her drink <s>kāpiśāyana</s> in the measure of two <s>palas</s>. This is the meaning.

children.text: tayā yoṣayā kāpiśāyane pīte sati uttarasūtreṇa pānajanyaṃ yat sukhaṃ tad darśayati ||
children.translated_text: When that woman has drunk <s>kāpiśāyana</s>, he shows, by the following sūtra, the pleasure produced by drinking.
'When sipping is being performed' is the phrase.

children.text: priyasakhīdvārā kriyamāṇe 'nuprāśane satīti jñeyam madāvirbhāveṇa anusaṃdhānābhāvāt nirbhedajanyā vyathā nānubhūyate ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It should be understood as 'when the sipping is being performed through a dear female friend.' Because intoxication has appeared, there is no awareness, and so the pain produced by piercing is not felt. This is the meaning.
He shows another benefit on the following day.
'On the following day' is the phrase.

children.text: varāṅgavidīrṇād anantaram uttarasmin ghasre dine asaṃbheditam iva avidīrṇam iva paridṛśyate varāṅgam idam eva upakārakāntaram ||
children.translated_text: After the noble part has been split, on the following day it appears as though not joined together, as though not split. This noble part itself is another auxiliary benefit.

children.text: yoṣāyā anuprāśanena taddvārā uttararūpe phalavaiśiṣṭyaṃ saṃpradarśayati ||
children.translated_text: By the woman’s drinking, and through that, he displays the excellence of the result in the subsequent form.
That is, when the playful activity is being performed.

children.text: uttararūpeṇa kriyamāṇe narmavyāpāre nidhuvanavyāpāre udañjer dhārṣṭyasya yaṣṭikāṇḍam iva atikaṭhinatāṃ samprāptasya meḍhrasya phalegrahir avandhyasāmarthyaṃ paridṛśyate ||
children.translated_text: When the playful activity is being performed in the subsequent form, namely the activity of intercourse, the fruitful and unfailing power of the penis is seen; it has attained extreme hardness, like a staff-section of <s>udañji</s>’s boldness.

children.text: etad uktaṃ bhavati kāpiśāyanasya anuprāśanamātreṇātisaṃkucitatvaṃ prāptasya yoṣāyāḥ varāṅgasya atidṛḍhatamasyāpy udañjeḥ varāṅgamukhavidīrṇane sāmarthyābhāvāt parābhavaṃ prāpta evety arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What is said is this: merely by drinking <s>kāpiśāyana</s>, the woman’s noble part becomes extremely contracted; therefore even the very firm noble part of <s>udañji</s>, lacking power to split the mouth of the noble part, is indeed defeated. This is the meaning.

children.text: sambhedite 'pi varāṅge kāpiśāyanaprāśanena atisaṃkocaṃ prāptasya yoṣāyāḥ varāṅgasya vivarakaraṇe udañjau mahatī vyathā prādurbhūyate iti bhāvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The sense is that, even when the noble part has been penetrated, great pain arises for <s>udañji</s> in making an opening in the woman’s noble part, which has become extremely contracted by drinking <s>kāpiśāyana</s>.

children.text: anena vākyena dvitīyavṛttāv api punaḥ yo 'nividīrṇasukhaṃ puruṣo 'nubhūyate iti tātparyārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By this sentence the intended meaning is that, in the second course also, the man experiences again the pleasure of one not yet pierced.

children.text: śyāmayā saha nirveśane ratisukhodbodhanaṃ vīryastambhanaṃ kālāvadhiṃ ca proktam upaśyāmayā saha krīḍane samupasthitau tatrāpi aireyasvīkaraṇasya atyāvaśyakatvenānuvidhānaṃ vidadhāti ||
children.translated_text: Having stated, in connection with settling down with the dark woman, the awakening of sexual pleasure, the restraint of semen, and the limit of time, he now prescribes, when play with the secondary dark woman has arisen, the observance of accepting <s>aireya</s> there too, because it is utterly necessary.
That is, 'with the secondary dark woman.'

children.text: aprāptayauvanābhiḥ saha bāhyatantre manīṣāyāḥ samupasthitau aṇumātraṃ tasyai prāśayitavyaṃ tāvanmātreṇaiva ubhayoḥ ānandasukhānulabdheḥ cumbanādivyāpāre anuvidhīyamāne alpasvīkāramātreṇa ānandānubhavadarśanāt na tatra ādhikyena pāśinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When intention has arisen in the external system with girls who have not reached youth, a minute amount should be given to her to drink. By just that much, the experience of pleasure and delight is obtained by both; since delight is seen through only a small acceptance when activities such as kissing are being performed, there is no need there for excess on the part of the noose-bearer.

children.text: ātmajāyāḥ svīkaraṇam iti hetuvādaṃ manasi nidhāya auttarīyaṃ sūtram anuśāsti ||
children.translated_text: Keeping in mind the causal argument that this is the acceptance of one’s own daughter, he teaches the subsequent sūtra.
That is, 'with those who have not reached youth.'

children.text: idānīm utkaṭayauvanāvasthāyām aireyaprāśanaṃ ratitantravilāse upadiśyate netarāvasthāyām upayogābhāvād anadhikāritvād ity ālocya dvitīyāvasthāyām atyāvaśyakatvam iti paurastyasūtreṇānudarśayati ||
children.translated_text: Now, considering that drinking <s>aireya</s> is taught in the sport of the sexual system only in the condition of intense youth, not in another condition because there is no use and no eligibility, he shows by the eastern sūtra that it is utterly necessary in the second condition.
That is, 'in that which is the base of the suffix -tīya.'

children.text: tīyapratyayasya prakṛtibhūtāyām avasthāyāṃ dvitīyāyām avasthāyāṃ dves tīya ity anena dviśabdāt tīyapratyaye sati dvitīyaśabdo niṣpadyate tasyām avasthāyāṃ kaśyasvīkaraṇasyātyāvaśyakatvam sati pūrvarūpasaṃyoge tādṛgavasthāvatyāḥ yoṣāyāḥ saṃnidhāne satīti jñeyam ||
children.translated_text: In the condition that is the base of the suffix -tīya, namely in the second condition: by the rule 'two plus tīya,' when the suffix -tīya is applied to the word <s>dvi</s>, the word <s>dvitīya</s> is formed. In that condition, the acceptance of <s>kaśya</s> is utterly necessary; it should be understood as applying when there is conjunction with the prior form, that is, when a woman possessing such a condition is present.

children.text: nanu dṛṣṭaprayojanam uddiśya svīkaraṇaṃ vidhīyate vā adṛṣṭaphalam uddiśya vā dṛṣṭaprayojanasyaivātrākāṅkṣitatvān nādṛṣṭaprayojanam uddiśyeti dṛṣṭaprayojanaṃ tu udañjidārḍhyapūrvarūpasya dṛṣṭaprayojanaṃ tu āsyorojādyavayaveṣu usrādhikyasyātyādhikyatvena saṃdarśanam etasya phalatritayasyānubhavārthaṃ dvitīyāvasthāvatā puruṣeṇa yoṣayā saha atyāvaśyakatvena sīdhugrahaṇaṃ rativilāsakāle sarvathaiva kartavyam ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But one may ask: is acceptance prescribed with a visible purpose in view, or with an unseen result in view? Since only a visible purpose is expected here, it is not with an unseen purpose in view. The visible purpose is the prior form of the firmness of <s>udañji</s>; and the visible purpose is also the display, in the mouth, breasts, and other limbs, of an excessive abundance of fluid. For the experience of this threefold result, a man in the second condition must by all means take liquor with a woman at the time of erotic play. This is the meaning.

children.text: saṃprasāraṇaviśiṣṭatīyapratyayasya prakṛtibhūtāyām avasthāyāṃ tu nātyāvaśyakam ity āha ||
children.translated_text: But in the condition that is the base of the suffix -tīya marked by vowel-expansion, it is not utterly necessary, he says.
That is, 'in the other condition.'

children.text: diṣṭakanyayā vyāptāyām avasthāyām urojandhayāyām avasthāyāṃ ca tasya prāśane nādhikārikatvam iti ||
children.translated_text: In the condition occupied by the fated maiden, and also in the condition of one whose breasts have dried up, there is no eligibility for his drinking it.
He presents two sūtras as the reason in both cases.
That is, 'because in the one case there is no full knowledge.'

children.text: ekatra paugaṇḍavayasaḥ puruṣakalpasya uttarasmin kāle upaśyāmayā samīkṛte anehasi andhasaḥ rasasya retasaḥ paripakvatāyāḥ abhāvāt tādṛkkarmādhikāre nādhikāritā ||
children.translated_text: In the one case, when the boyish age of a male person is matched later with the secondary dark woman, there is no eligibility for authority in such an act, because the fluid, the juice, namely semen, has not reached maturity.
That is, 'in the other case.'

children.text: jīrṇāvasthāyām api tadānīṃ diṣṭakanyayā saha atinarmavyavasāyena sarvāsām indriyavṛttānāṃ svakīyapravṛttau kṣīṇataratvasya dṛśyamānatvān nādhikārakatvam ||
children.translated_text: Even in the aged condition, at that time, because all the activities of the senses are seen to be very much diminished in their own operation through excessive engagement in play with the fated maiden, there is no eligibility for authority.

children.text: bālasya tathā jarāvataḥ puruṣasya ubhayoḥ narmakarmādhikāre nādhikāriteti sūtradvayasya tātparyārthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The intended meaning of the two sūtras is that both a boy and an aged man have no eligibility for authority in the act of play.

children.text: kāraṇarūpopādhau satyāṃ kāryarūpasyopādheḥ anudarśanam iti nyāyena padmāyāḥ anugraheṇa paripūritānāṃ sārvabhaumādīnām eva anayā puṣpadhanuṣaḥ saraṇyā anuvartanaṃ sārvakālikaṃ nityakarmādhikāravat yuktataraṃ nānyeṣām iti prakaraṇopasaṃhāram anudarśayati ||
children.translated_text: By the principle that, when the causal condition exists, the condition in the form of the effect is shown, he indicates the conclusion of the topic: only universal sovereigns and others who are filled by the favor of <s>Padmā</s> may most fittingly follow this path of the flower-bowed god at all times, as though having eligibility for a perpetual rite, and not others.
That is, 'of people who possess the beloved of <s>Hari</s>.'

children.text: nanu ekatra vidhāne niṣedhavākyaṃ kutra vidhīyate ity uktaṃ cet pūrvoktajanapratiyogikeṣu pravartate ity āśayenāha ||
children.translated_text: If it is asked, 'When an injunction is made in one case, where is the prohibitive statement prescribed?', then, with the intention that it applies to those contrasted with the people previously mentioned, he says:
That is, 'of the others than those.'
The meaning is: of those who are devoid of the wealth of the milk-ocean-born goddess.

children.text: nanu atyāvaśyakatvena īdṛkkarmavidhānaṃ kutrābhivyāptam iti cet tat sthānaṃ saṃpradarśayati ||
children.translated_text: Now, if it is asked, 'Where is the prescription of such an act included, since it is utterly necessary?', he shows that place.
'By exclusion' is the phrase.

children.text: pariśeṣasya bhāvaḥ pāriśeṣyaṃ tasmāt niṣedhavyāptyā rahitāt pārāvāratanūjayā saṃyukteṣv eva kāpi śāyanasvīkaraṇaśāstrasya pravṛttiḥ anirvacanīyānandabodhāya pravartata ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pāriśeṣya</s> means the state of what remains over; therefore, because it is not pervaded by prohibition, the activity of the śāstra concerning acceptance of kāpiśāyana operates only among those joined with the daughter of the ocean, for the awakening of indescribable bliss. This is the meaning.
He indicates another opinion.
'On the days of the offspring of <s>Gotrā</s>' is the phrase.

children.text: gotrāyāḥ apatyaṃ tasya ghasraṃ dinaṃ tasmin dine anutarṣasvīkaraṇam iti mṛkaṇḍatanūjasya matam ||
children.translated_text: The offspring of <s>Gotrā</s>, and its <s>ghasra</s>, day: on that day there is acceptance of <s>anutarṣa</s>. This is the opinion of the son of <s>Mṛkaṇḍu</s>.
He shows the opinion of the others by the following sūtra.
'On the days of <s>Kāvya</s>' is the phrase.

children.text: śukro daityaguruḥ kāvya iti kośābhidhānāt ghasro dināhanī vā tv ity amaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Since the lexicon states, '<s>Śukra</s>, the preceptor of the Daityas, is <s>Kāvya</s>,' and <s>Amara</s> says, '<s>ghasra</s> means day or daytime.'
'<s>Suratha</s> and the others': by the word 'others' the Vaiśya is included.
He shows the intended sense of the restrictive injunction.
'Of the two sentences' is the phrase.

children.text: śaktyupāsanāvatām evāyaṃ niyamaḥ yat ghasradvaye 'py anuvartanaṃ taditareṣāṃ janānāṃ pralambaghnamatānuyāyināṃ tu yathākālopadeśa iti na ghasradvaye parisaṃkhyānam ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: This rule belongs only to those who practice the worship of <s>Śakti</s>, namely that it continues on both days. But for other people, those who follow the doctrine of the slayer of <s>Pralamba</s>, the instruction is according to the proper time; thus there is no restrictive enumeration to the two days. This is the meaning.
Moreover:
'In the second varṇa' is the phrase.

children.text: kṣatrajātau dvitīyavarṇe kāpiśāyanasvīkaraṇavidhānaṃ sārvakālikaṃ tāmasīprakṛteḥ upāsanādhikāravatāṃ nirantaraṃ kādambarasvīkaraṇaṃ kartavyatvenābhimatam ||
children.translated_text: In the kṣatra class, the second varṇa, the prescription for accepting kāpiśāyana is valid at all times; for those whose tamasic nature gives them eligibility for worship, continual acceptance of kādambara is considered something that must be done.

children.text: aparokṣānubhavena tatsvarūpānudarśane upādānakāraṇatvāt ātmabhuvaḥ tanoḥ upāsanādhikāravat na ghasrayoḥ anuvartanam ||
children.translated_text: Since direct experience is the material cause for the manifestation of its true nature, there is no continuation on the two days as there is eligibility for worship of the body of the Self-born one.
He lays down the restrictive injunction for the varṇa taught by instruction.
'Because of the sacrifice' is the phrase.

children.text: vājapeye surāgrahān gṛhṇāti sautrāmaṇyāṃ surāgrahān gṛhṇātīti vākyadvayena prathamavarṇikasya yathāvācanikam eva grahaṇaprāśaneṣu ādhikāriko vidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: By the two sentences, 'In the <s>Vājapeya</s> he takes cups of surā' and 'In the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s> he takes cups of surā,' for a member of the first varṇa there is an authoritative injunction, exactly according to the wording, concerning taking and drinking the cups.

children.text: tathā cāyam arthaḥ vājapeye tu grahaṇamātrasyaivābhyanujñānaṃ prāśanābhyanujñānaṃ tu tṛtīyavarṇasyaiva tathā cānuśravikavākyaṃ vimāthaṃ kurvate vājasṛta iti ||
children.translated_text: Accordingly, this is the meaning: in the <s>Vājapeya</s>, permission is given only for the mere taking of the cup; permission to drink belongs only to the third varṇa. Thus the Vedic sentence says, 'The winners of the prize make the <s>vimātha</s>.'

children.text: sautrāmaṇyāṃ tu yāgakartur eva prāśanaṃ nigamavākyenābhidhīyate netareṣām ṛtvijām tatrāpy āghrāṇenaiva prāśanapratipattir iti matāntaram iti ṛṣyantarāṇāṃ vacanam iti ||
children.translated_text: But in the <s>Sautrāmaṇī</s>, the Vedic sentence states that only the performer of the sacrifice drinks, not the other officiating priests. Even there, according to another opinion, drinking is understood only as smelling it; so say the words of other seers.

children.text: sārvakālikābhyanujñānaṃ tu rasādhipatīnām eva nānyeṣāṃ janānām iti prakaraṇārtham upasaṃharati ||
children.translated_text: He concludes the topic by saying that permission for all times belongs only to lords of rasa, not to other people.
'Of those who hold lordship over regions, districts, and the like' is the phrase.

children.text: alpaviṣayasya śāsanakartṝṇāṃ rājñāṃ lokamātur anugraheṇa paripūritānāṃ sīdhugrahaṇena vilāsānubhavaḥ vilāsānām anubhavanaṃ sārvakālikam na surathavaiśyādīnāṃ matam anusṛtya pravartanam ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For kings who are rulers of limited domains, made complete by the favor of the Mother of the World, the experience of pleasure through taking sīdhu, that is, the enjoyment of pleasures, is valid at all times; it is not a practice undertaken by following the doctrine concerning <s>Suratha</s>, the Vaiśya, and the rest. This is the meaning.
He shows the restrictive injunction concerning the drinking of young women.
'In the company of her own beloved' is the phrase.

children.text: nidhuvanakāle eva svapatibhiḥ sārdhaṃ kādambarasvīkaraṇasyābhyanujñānaṃ netarāvasthāyāṃ kutaḥ upayogābhāvāt niṣphalaprayāse svīkaraṇasya vaiyarthyāpatteḥ ||
children.translated_text: Only at the time of lovemaking is permission given for accepting kādambara together with their own husbands, and not in any other condition, because there is no use for it; if the effort is fruitless, the acceptance would become pointless.
Even within the restrictive injunction he adds a further particular qualification.
'Even there, only in the sacrifices of the one not born from another' is the phrase.

children.text: ananyajena kriyamāṇeṣu makheṣv eva atyāvaśyakatvena anutarṣasvīkaraṇavidhānaṃ netaratra tadatiriktakāleṣv iti ||
children.translated_text: Only in rites being performed by the one not born from another is the injunction to accept <s>anutarṣa</s> made as utterly necessary, and not elsewhere, at times other than that.

children.text: yoṣāyāḥ atra yoṣāsaṃgraheṇa upaśyāmādīnām eva saṃgrahaḥ na vibhraṃśitadvitīyāvasthānām āsyapadmena prāśanaṃ tu atyutkṛṣṭaphalaviśeṣāntaraṃ niścitya atyāvaśyakatvena prāśanam anudarśayati ||
children.translated_text: Here, in the inclusion of a woman, only <s>Upaśyāmā</s> and the others are included, not those who have fallen away from the second state. But drinking with the lotus of the mouth is a further, supremely excellent special result; having determined this, he shows that the drinking is utterly necessary.
'With the lotus of a woman's mouth' is the phrase.

children.text: yoṣāyāḥ āsyapadmena prāśane kriyamāṇe yathecchikī bhāṣāyāḥ anusphurtir bhavatīty arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When drinking is performed with the lotus of a woman's mouth, there arises a spontaneous manifestation of whatever language one desires. This is the meaning.

children.text: anena vākyena śravaṇādivyavasāyarahite 'pi jane niṣprayāsenaiva tridaśānāṃ gīḥ svamukhāt prādurbhūyata ity arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By this sentence the meaning is that even in a person lacking the effort of hearing and the like, the speech of the gods appears from his own mouth without effort.

children.text: anyad apy utkṛṣṭataraṃ phalaviśeṣāntaraṃ svīkāramātreṇa saṃpradarśayati ||
children.translated_text: He shows another still more excellent special result from the mere acceptance.
'From the thousand-petaled mouth of <s>Śyāmā</s>' is the phrase.

children.text: śyāmāyāḥ kamalaprasūnāt anuprāśanaṃ pratyakṣānubhavena sākṣāt mūlaprakṛteḥ svarūpānudarśane hetuḥ kāraṇam iti tayā saha saṃprāśane kriyamāṇe kṛtsnasya prapañcasya kāraṇabhūtāyāḥ mūlaprakṛteḥ sākaṃ saṃgato bhavati ||
children.translated_text: Drinking from the lotus blossom of <s>Śyāmā</s> is, by direct experience, the means, the cause, for the immediate manifestation of the true nature of primordial nature; when drinking together with her is performed, one becomes united with primordial nature, the cause of the whole manifest world.

children.text: yad vā tatsvarūpaṃ sākṣād avyavadhānena paśyatīty arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Or else, the meaning is that one sees that true nature directly and without mediation.

children.text: anena vākyena sāyujyādikaṃ phalam api nirāyāsena prāpnotīty arthaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By this sentence the meaning is that one also attains the result of union and the like without difficulty.
At the time of love, the drinking of sīdhu is to be done; this is taught by the injunction.
Before that, the description of play stated in the science of love is to be followed.

children.text: tat sarvaṃ tu prakartavyaṃ yoṣāyāḥ sukhalabdhaye ||
children.translated_text: All of that, however, is to be performed for the obtaining of pleasure by the woman.
For the sake of easy understanding even for himself, and for the sake of the cause of producing offspring.

children.text: phaladvayaṃ sa prāpnoti prajāṃ kāmasukhaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: He obtains a twofold fruit: progeny, and also the pleasure of desire.

children.text: urvaśīlokam āpnoti antakāle tu saḥ pumān ||
children.translated_text: And at the time of death that man reaches the world of <s>Urvaśī</s>.

children.text: iti śrīmahārājarṣivaryeṇa purūravasā viracitaṃ kāmijanānāṃ vinodāya rativilāsāṅgabhūtaṃ kādambarasvīkaraṇasūtraṃ savyākhyānaṃ samāptim agamat ||
children.translated_text: Thus the <s>Kādambarasvīkaraṇasūtra</s>, together with its commentary, composed by the illustrious foremost royal sage <s>Purūravas</s> for the amusement of amorous people and forming a component of erotic dalliance, has come to completion.
